Yonder
yŏn´der
adv. (at a distance within view; over there; rendering Hebrew koh and Greek ekei)
Old English geond, through, beyond. The word points; it is spoken by a man who can see the place he means and is about to go to it.

Biblical Definition

Abraham at the foot of Moriah: “Abide ye here with the ass; and I and the lad will go yonder and worship, and come again to you” (Gen 22:5). The Lord at Gethsemane: “Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder” (Mat 26:36). Balaam to Balak: “Stand here by thy burnt offering, while I meet the LORD yonder” (Num 23:15). Elisha seeing the Shunammite: “Behold, yonder is that Shunammite” (2Ki 4:25). And of faith: “If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove” (Mat 17:20). Reuben and Gad would not inherit “on yonder side Jordan” (Num 32:19).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines yonder as at a distance within view.

expand to see more

YONDER, a. Being at a distance within view; as yonder hill.

YONDER, adv. At a distance within view.

Key Scripture

Gen 22:5 — "And Abraham said unto his young men, Abide ye here with the ass; and I and the lad will go yonder and worship, and come again to you."

Mat 26:36 — "Then cometh Jesus with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and saith unto the disciples, Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder."

Num 23:15 — "And he said unto Balak, Stand here by thy burnt offering, while I meet the LORD yonder."

Mat 17:20 — "And Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you."

2Ki 4:25 — "So she went and came unto the man of God to mount Carmel. And it came to pass, when the man of God saw her afar off, that he said to Gehazi his servant, Behold, yonder is that Shunammite:"

Modern Corruption

Abraham's come again to you is read as a kind lie to the servants, and Hebrews says it was the arithmetic of the resurrection.

expand to see more

Genesis 22:5 is often read as a father sparing his servants the truth. Abraham said we will go yonder and worship, and we will come again — carrying the knife and the fire and the boy who was to be the sacrifice — and Hebrews 11:19 gives the plain reading: he accounted that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead. The father who went yonder expected to come back with the son, by resurrection if by nothing else, because the promise was in that son and the promise could not fail. Two thousand years later another Son said to His disciples, “Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder,” and went a stone's cast further into the same obedience; and He too came again to them. Yonder in Scripture is where a man goes alone to worship with a knife at his side, and it is not the end of the story.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew koh (H3541), thus, here, there, yonder; Greek ekei (G1563), there, in that place.

expand to see more

Hebrew ad-koh (H3541) — as far as yonder; Genesis 22:5; koh, Numbers 23:15; halom (H1973), Numbers 16:37.

Greek ekei (G1563) — there, yonder; Matthew 17:20, 26:36.

Usage

"“I and the lad will go yonder and worship, and come again to you” — the resurrection counted on before it happened."

"“Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder” — the Son on His Moriah."

"“Remove hence to yonder place” — faith as a grain of mustard seed."
